title: Attenuated warm-pool smoothing and utilization exposer for dedicated fleets
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Context: Dedicated fleet warm pools are currently susceptible to short-lived microbursts: a handful of tenants generate transient spikes that cause the warm-pool controller to over-allocate headroom, inflate cost, and produce noisy per-tenant utilization metrics. This PR introduces an attenuated smoothing policy for warm-pool sizing and a lightweight utilization exposer that decouples instantaneous spikes from the long-running reservation logic. Motivation: reduce oscillation-driven overprovisioning, improve stability for tenant SLAs, and provide clearer telemetry to platform teams so they can tune reservations and burst contracts. Changes in this PR (high level): - Introduce an attenuated smoothing window with configurable decay factors and min/max headroom bounds. The algorithm applies exponential decay to short spikes while allowing sustained demand to grow warm pool capacity. - Add microburst detector that can tag allocations as transient (microburst) vs sustained; microburst signals are retained short-term and influence only ephemeral warm allocations. - Expose per-tenant utilization summaries (P50/P95/P99 token throughput and burst incidence rate) to telemetry pipeline with a compact protobuf payload for ingestion. - Split warm-pool decision path: "elastic" (longer smoothing) vs "ephemeral" (microburst buffer) to keep committed reservations stable. - Add feature flag and runtime knobs: warm_pool.smoothing.enabled, warm_pool.smoothing.decay_tau_ms, warm_pool.ephemeral_budget_pct, telemetry.util_bucket_window_ms. Checklist: - [x] Core algorithm and controller changes implemented - [x] Unit tests for smoothing kernel and microburst tagging - [x] Integration test that simulates mixed sustained + bursty tenants and validates headroom change bounds - [x] Telemetry schema and exporter implementation - [x] Docs: operator guide and runtime knobs - [x] Feature-flag gating for staged rollout Commits (summary): - init: add smoothing kernel and interfaces (pkg/autoscaler/smoothing.go) - controller: wire smoothing into warm-pool reconciler and split decision path (pkg/autoscaler/controller.go) - telemetry: add utilization exposer and protobuf (internal/metrics/utilization_exposer.go, proto/utilization.proto) - exporter: push compact metrics to metrics pipeline with sampling (cmd/dedicated/telemetry/exporter.go) - tests: unit and integration harness (tests/integration/warm_pool_smoothing_test.go) - docs: operational guide and examples (docs/operational/warm-pool.md) Files changed (high-level): pkg/autoscaler/smoothing.go, pkg/autoscaler/controller.go, internal/metrics/utilization_exposer.go, proto/utilization.proto, cmd/dedicated/telemetry/exporter.go, docs/operational/warm-pool.md Why this is safe: - Backwards compatible: smoothing is behind warm_pool.smoothing.enabled (default=false for initial rollout). - Telemetry schema is additive; consumers that don't parse the new proto will ignore the new field. - Behavior can be reverted by toggling feature flag or adjusting decay_tau_ms to a neutral value. Testing notes: - Local integration harness simulates 100 tenants with 10% producing 2s microbursts and confirms <7% warm-pool capacity change compared to baseline. - Unit tests cover edge cases including zero traffic, sustained ramp, and pathological bursts. Review conversation summary: - Ethan: requested clearer bounds on min/max headroom and unit for decay_tau_ms. I added validation and docs explaining units are milliseconds and provided reasonable defaults (decay_tau_ms=5000ms, min_headroom=1, max_headroom=5). - Miguel: asked for an additional metric to report number of microburst-tagged allocations per minute; added microburst_alloc_count and unit test. - Ava: suggested moving the telemetry exporter to a separate goroutine to avoid blocking reconciler; refactored exporter to use buffered channel and background worker and added backpressure handling. CI / checks: - CI run 1: go vet + unit tests (flaky DB connection in test harness) -> failed; reran. - CI run 2: full unit + integration (short) -> pass. Observability: - dashboards: added warm-pool smoothing dashboard panel (docs/operational/warm-pool.md) showing headroom, microburst rate, and utilization percentiles. - Alerts: recommend adding alert warm_pool.unexpected_growth if headroom increases >50% over 5m window. Migration/rollout plan: - Stage 1 (dev): enable smoothing for dev clusters for 48h; monitor microburst_alloc_count and headroom trend. - Stage 2 (staging): enable for 1 week, bounded by feature-flag autoswitch if warm_pool.unexpected_growth fires. - Stage 3 (canary->prod): gradual ramp to 10% fleets, then 30%, with automated rollback criteria. Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals and green CI. Merge commit: abc123def4567890. Release notes: Added attenuated warm-pool smoothing to reduce reactive overprovisioning from short-lived tenant microbursts; introduced per-tenant utilization exposer (P50/P95/P99 + microburst incidence); feature flag warm_pool.smoothing.enabled controls rollout. Followups / TODOs: - ENG-6012: surface per-tenant utilization in Console route. - ENG-5687: tune default decay_tau_ms via A/B tests across dev fleets.
